review_notes: I read the whole file and checked how its new definitions (symmetrize, openCube, formMatrix, periodicExtR, periodicMatrixExt) are used here and in Compact/Main.lean. The file declares no simp lemmas or attributes. I found no competing rules, wrong orientations or loops. The findings are about missing canonical entry and membership lemmas for the new definitions. Each definition is unfolded by name inside `simp [...]` calls, both in this file and downstream. I did not run Lean, so I can't say how well the proposed lemmas would work as simp lemmas. The `periodicExtR` and `periodicMatrixExt` unfoldings are weaker cases, so I left them out.

findings.excerpt:
def symmetrize (A : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℝ) : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℝ :=
  (1 / 2 : ℝ) • (A + Aᵀ)
findings.problem: `symmetrize` has no canonical simp lemma for its entries or transpose. Every proof about it unfolds the definition by name, with `simp [symmetrize, ...]` at lines 173 and 187, and `rw [symmetrize, ...]` in `symmetrize_eq_self`. Unfolding exposes `(1/2) • (A + Aᵀ)`, so simp then needs `transpose_add`, `add_comm` and a manual `ring` to reach the entrywise form `(A i j + A j i)/2`. The same entrywise statement is restated by hand in `quadForm_symmetrize` (the `h` have) and in `contDiff_symmetrize` (the `change` to `(1/2) * (A i j + A j i)`).
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] theorem symmetrize_apply (A) (i j) : symmetrize A i j = (A i j + A j i) / 2`, or with `(1/2) * (...)` to match the file's usage. Add `@[simp] theorem transpose_symmetrize (A) : (symmetrize A)ᵀ = symmetrize A`, or `symmetrize_isSymm.eq`. Stating `symmetrize_eq_self` as a simp lemma with hypothesis `hA : A.IsSymm` is also possible. The existing proofs can then use these lemmas instead of unfolding `symmetrize`.
findings.benefit: Proofs about `symmetrize` work with a stable entrywise normal form instead of the internal `(1/2) • (A + Aᵀ)` encoding. The proofs of `symmetrize_isSymm`, `quadForm_symmetrize` and `contDiff_symmetrize` get shorter and no longer depend on how the definition is written.

findings.excerpt: def openCube (N : ℕ) : Set (Fin N → ℝ) := {x | ∀ j, |x j| < Real.pi}
findings.problem: There is no membership lemma such as `mem_openCube`. Downstream code unfolds the definition inside simp, for example `simp [openCube, Set.mem_iInter]` in `isOpen_openCube`. Simp then has to push set-builder membership through the unfolded definition. In this file, `periodicExtR_eq_self_of_mem` and `periodicMatrixExt_eq_of_mem` state hypotheses as `x ∈ openCube N` but state closed-cube membership as a bare `∀ j, |x j| ≤ Real.pi`, so the two cube notions have no common simp-friendly interface.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] theorem mem_openCube {x : Fin N → ℝ} : x ∈ openCube N ↔ ∀ j, |x j| < Real.pi := Iff.rfl`. `openCube` can then stay a plain def that is not unfolded elsewhere.
findings.benefit: Callers rewrite membership with one canonical lemma, so proofs such as `isOpen_openCube` no longer unfold the definition. If the definition of `openCube` changes later, only this lemma needs updating.

findings.excerpt: Matrix.of fun i j => B (EuclideanSpace.single i 1) (EuclideanSpace.single j 1)
findings.problem: `formMatrix` has no entry lemma `formMatrix B i j = B (single i 1) (single j 1)`. The lemma named `formMatrix_apply` is the bilinear evaluation `B a b = a ⬝ᵥ (formMatrix B).mulVec b`. It is not simp-suitable as stated, and it is only used for `rw`. Entry-level reasoning therefore unfolds the definition inside simp, in `formMatrix_posDef` (`simp [formMatrix, Matrix.transpose_apply, hsymm]`) and in Main.lean's `hmsymm`, which has the same simp call. `contDiff_formMatrix` uses a `change` to the unfolded form.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] theorem formMatrix_entry (B) (i j) : formMatrix B i j = B (EuclideanSpace.single i 1) (EuclideanSpace.single j 1) := rfl`. Optionally add a simp lemma for `(formMatrix B)ᵀ` under a symmetry hypothesis. Rename the evaluation lemma or document that it is a `rw`-only lemma, so the name `formMatrix_apply` does not suggest an entry simp lemma.
findings.benefit: Callers get a canonical entry rewrite without `simp [formMatrix]`. This also removes the ambiguity of the name `formMatrix_apply`, which currently names a non-simp evaluation identity.
